title: All About Woodlice
checkpoint: Phase 5 continues (School readiness) — non-fiction, real facts about woodlice.
note_for_grown_ups: Phase 5 continues (School readiness) — non-fiction, real facts about woodlice.

pages.text: A little bug sits on the wall top.
pages.illustration: A small grey woodlouse resting on the flat top of an old stone garden wall.

pages.text: A bug has a hard, bumpy shell.
pages.illustration: A close-up of the woodlouse showing its segmented, bumpy grey shell.

pages.text: A bug has lots of little legs.
pages.illustration: An underside view of the woodlouse showing its many small legs.

pages.text: A bug can curl into a ball.
pages.illustration: The woodlouse tightly curled up into a small round ball shape.

pages.text: A bug likes damp, dark spots.
pages.illustration: The woodlouse tucked into a damp, shadowy crack in the stone wall.

pages.text: A bug hides in the crack in the wall.
pages.illustration: A narrow crack in the wall where several woodlice are tucked in close together.

pages.text: A bug eats soft, wet wood and a leaf.
pages.illustration: A woodlouse nibbling at a piece of old, damp, rotting leaf.

pages.text: Nell spots the bug on the wall top.
pages.illustration: Nell the bee hovering just above the wall, looking down at the woodlouse.

pages.text: Nell looks at it curl into a ball.
pages.illustration: Nell the bee watching closely as the woodlouse curls up tight.

pages.text: Bugs like this help keep the garden tidy.
pages.illustration: Nell the bee and the woodlouse together on the wall top, the garden visible behind them.
